PullRequest.Title: agentHost: serve Dev Containers on the editor's local endpoint
PullRequest.Body:
Dev Tunnel and SSH clients that choose **Use Remote VS Code** reach the remote window's agent host through its local endpoint. That endpoint's handler is created with `allowExtensionMethods: false`, which, besides the host-control methods, also skips the Dev Container protocol. Such hosts therefore advertise neither `vscode.devContainers` nor `vscode.devContainerEnvironments`, so the Agents window offers no Dev Container execution and no **Create Dev Container** for them, even when the host has Docker. The same host connected with **Run in the Background** (standalone agent host) offers both, since it runs the same runtime and Dev Container service.

Changes:
- Add `allowDevContainers` to the protocol handler config, defaulting to `allowExtensionMethods`.
- Enable it for the editor's local endpoint only. The renderer's MessagePort handler is unchanged; the window runs its own Dev Containers through the shared process.
- `shutdown`, diagnostics, sandbox certificate changes, Copilot extension management and GitHub environment sharing remain unavailable on that endpoint.

Note: like other remote hosts, this endpoint resolves `docker` from the agent host's environment rather than `dev.containers.dockerPath`.

Testing:
- New `protocolServerHandler` test: a handler with `allowExtensionMethods: false, allowDevContainers: true` advertises both Dev Container capabilities and answers `isDockerAvailable`, while `shutdown` still returns MethodNotFound and Copilot extensions are not advertised. It fails without the handler change.
- `protocolServerHandler.test.ts` (562 passing), `typecheck-client`, oxlint.

Scenarios.Scenario: Editor Agent Host startup and initialization of local-endpoint clients, versus the renderer MessagePort and standalone hosts
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Renderer protocol registration still precedes external-endpoint startup. The changed external handler creates a DevContainerAgentHostProtocol only during client initialization; its constructor allocates two maps and service-event subscriptions, without launching containers, probing Docker, or awaiting I/O. The renderer retains allowExtensionMethods:false without the new override.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Start the external socket endpoint and publish endpoint metadata.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One endpoint setup and publication per editor Agent Host startup.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same endpoint setup, separate handler, and metadata publication occurred before the change.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: External ingress availability waits for setup; renderer channel registration already completed.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Expose the renderer MessagePort data plane.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One registration per utility-process Agent Host.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical ordering and configuration; the new flag is applied only to the external handler.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Renderer connects independently of external endpoint startup.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One small protocol adapter per initialized external transport; zero adapters for the unchanged renderer path. No multiplication by sessions, workspaces, or history entries.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Existing startup ordering is unchanged. Protocol initialization performs only synchronous bounded adapter setup; no new asynchronous boundary is inserted into the handshake.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The Dev Container service was already injected into ProtocolServerHandler before the PR. Initialization does not invoke its lazy executable, environment, or certificate resolution. Adapter subscriptions are disposed with initializationDisposables on rollback or connection disposal.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: changed config, handler constructor, initialization call sites, adapter constructor, and transport cleanup were traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact connection counts and adapter allocation sizes are not measured.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: no heavyweight eager work or lost cleanup; renderer startup is unchanged.

Scenarios.Scenario: Docker capability discovery and Dev Container choices for SSH/Tunnel hosts using Use Remote VS Code
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A newly advertised capability permits asynchronous Docker discovery after host initialization. Create Dev Container visibility waits for the discovery result. Workspace-specific availability first checks the two supported configuration paths and then Docker availability; ordinary host connection and picker rendering do not await these checks.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send isDockerAvailable over the existing source-host protocol connection.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One discovery RPC per host connection object, with pending, positive, negative, and failed results retained by _dockerChecks; workspace checks can additionally issue one RPC per uncached configured workspace.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The editor's external endpoint did not advertise the capability, so these gated checks were skipped for that endpoint. Other supported remote hosts already used this path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Controls feature availability, not completion of the source-host handshake.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Find docker in the host environment using filesystem existence/stat checks.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One coalesced PATH search per host service and configured Docker path, proportional to PATH entries and Windows executable extensions; warm and negative cached results perform no new search. No Docker subprocess is launched by availability checking.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: This lazy lookup was unreachable through the editor external endpoint's Dev Container RPCs; the implementation and cache already existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Only the cold Docker-availability result waits for the search.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve the two candidate devcontainer configuration files through the existing remote file provider.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two existence checks per uncached distinct provider/workspace key, issued together; picker duplicates share the cached in-flight promise.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The absent capability short-circuited this container-specific availability path for the editor endpoint. Remote filesystem transport itself was already available.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Workspace container-choice availability waits for these checks; results asynchronously refresh the picker.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: H distinct configured connected hosts for environment discovery and W distinct provider/workspace keys for workspace availability. Docker RPCs for workspace checks occur only for workspaces with configuration.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Picker availability uses a shared Limiter(4); each job issues two configuration checks in parallel. Distinct host discovery RPCs can overlap, but repeated checks for the same connection are coalesced and all Docker lookups within a service share one promise.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Host discovery caches pending/success/false/error-as-unavailable by connection identity and removes unconfigured hosts. Docker executable resolution caches the promise including undefined. Picker availability caches promises, booleans, and errors by provider plus normalized workspace URI, with existing invalidation and explicit error retry.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: capability gates, client RPC adapter, service lookup cache, file-provider boundary, and picker limiter/cache were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Host/workspace counts, network RTT, and slow PATH filesystem prevalence are not measured.
Scenarios.Verdict: No high-confidence regression: enabling the feature adds bounded, cached, asynchronous availability work without moving heavyweight container startup onto rendering or general initialization.

Scenarios.Scenario: First prompt in a remote workspace container, explicit Create Dev Container, and reconnecting stored remote environments
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Workspace launches request trust before invoking the launcher. Container preparation, CLI setup, endpoint selection, and relay establishment must finish before container sessions can proceed. New environments are explicitly created; stored remote environments follow source-host connection changes through existing reconciliation. Unrelated source-host session listing does not await these launches.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Receive a container-connect RPC and, for workspace containers, request workspace trust over the existing connection.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One connect RPC per effective launch and one trust request per workspace launch; image-based environments do not request host-folder trust.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Dev Container methods were unavailable on the editor endpoint; supported standalone hosts already followed the same request path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required before that container's launch can continue.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Run bundled devcontainer CLI and Docker preparation, configuration, container startup, shell setup, endpoint discovery, and one persistent devcontainer-exec relay.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: A staged command sequence per effective source launch, with optional lifecycle/user-state commands. Environment volume/container discovery is scoped to that environment; no launch is issued per session-history item.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: These commands could not be requested through the editor endpoint. The launcher sequence, per-source sequencer, cancellation, and relay implementation are unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks readiness of the selected or restored container only.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Prepare cached environment configuration and certificate bundles for CLI children.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Configuration preparation per environment launch; certificate normalization/cache-file checks per environment resolution, with certificate loading coalesced by the proxy resolver and content-addressed bundle writes skipped on cache hits.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Existing service work becomes reachable from this endpoint; its frequency within each launch and cache policies are unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Completes before the corresponding CLI command; not performed merely by adapter construction or Docker availability discovery.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Download a matching VS Code CLI on cache miss and obtain container images as needed by Docker/devcontainer startup.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: CLI download only when the executable/shared cache cannot serve the required commit; image transfer depends on the Docker image cache. Warm launches reuse the matching executable and live Agent Host endpoint where available.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Unavailable through the editor endpoint; the same existing cold/warm installation and image behavior applied to supported standalone hosts.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cold container readiness waits for required downloads.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One launch per requested workspace or environment, or E stored environments belonging to a reconnected host. Repeated attempts for one environment share state.pending; operations for the same source key are serialized.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: DevContainerAgentHostService uses SequencerByKey for each workspace/environment source, not a global limiter. Distinct stored environments can reconnect concurrently; state.pending coalesces duplicate environment connects and each environment has its own operations sequencer. This scheduling architecture is unchanged.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Executable and shell-environment resolution are shared. Native certificates are loaded once and client certificates once per provider connection. Certificate files are content-addressed. Environment volumes, Docker images, shared CLI/server caches, matching CLI executables, and live Agent Host endpoints are reused. Existing failure/cancellation cleanup remains in place.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: launch ownership, environment reconciliation, sequencers, subprocess creation, cold/warm installer behavior, and cancellation cleanup were traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Cold build/download cost, number of stored environments, and aggregate host resource contention are not measured. Distinct-source concurrency remains an existing subsystem characteristic.
Scenarios.Verdict: No qualifying diff-introduced performance bug: the PR exposes the existing required launch workflow, without adding extra launch stages, defeating reuse, or changing scheduling per effective source.

Scenarios.Scenario: Container protocol traffic, disconnect/cancellation, and explicit stop/removal
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Container messages traverse the existing source connection and the devcontainer-exec relay. Disconnect cancels active work and disposes the relay; explicit stop/removal awaits source-key-serialized Docker lifecycle operations. These operations are not part of editor startup or workspace picker rendering.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Wrap container messages in source-host RPCs/notifications and forward them to or from the relay WebSocket.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One wrapper per actual container message; notifications are forwarded only to the adapter owning the connection ID, not to every client.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Container relaying was unavailable on the editor endpoint; the same framing/forwarding implementation already served other supported hosts.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Affects active container message delivery only.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Kill disposed relay subprocesses; inspect active container sessions and stop/remove requested containers or environment volumes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One relay disposal per active connection. Workspace lifecycle typically performs a session-check Docker exec and one stop/rm command; environment removal uses scoped lookup commands and grouped rm calls for matching IDs/volumes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Unavailable through this endpoint; underlying disposal, lifecycle grouping, and per-source ordering are unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Disconnect releases resources immediately; explicit lifecycle actions wait for their Docker commands.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Remove an explicitly deleted environment's cached configuration directory.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One recursive removal for the selected environment.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same existing cleanup became accessible through the newly enabled endpoint.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Part of explicit environment deletion only.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: M messages/bytes for active container connections; C active relays on disconnect; lifecycle work for the selected workspace/environment and its matching containers/volumes.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Same-source lifecycle actions share the launcher's SequencerByKey. Disconnecting several active relays may overlap but does not start replacement relays. Message forwarding filters by ownership; no new broadcast fan-out is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Connection maps are removed on disconnect, failure, or close. Protocol adapters are owned by transport initializationDisposables; closing the transport disposes subscriptions and disconnects started launches. Launcher disposable maps release relay processes and stores. Lifecycle operations reuse recorded container IDs and group matching resources.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: transport-close disposal, protocol ownership maps, service cleanup, relay disposal, and grouped lifecycle operations were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Traffic volume, container process counts in the existing session scan, and Docker shutdown duration are unmeasured.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable retention, cleanup, serialization, or boundary-fan-out regression. Existing behavior is exposed on another endpoint without increasing per-message copies or losing resource ownership.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance-review pass over the complete four-file inventory and every diff page against fd63bb42c4411ff81c4054d1b8d60a554baf8249. Traced initialization, capability discovery, picker availability, launch/restoration, relay traffic, and cleanup. No high-confidence actionable performance regressions or concrete performance-regression fixes identified. Static read-only analysis; durations and prevalence were not profiled.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
